title: Build the autonomous tree
summary: In Arbor: drive both paths, ask for AIM and wait for it with a time limit, shoot, wait, and stop.

say.never:
Your routine is a **behavior tree** in the file `PickupAndScore.xml`, and you build it in the **Arbor** pane by dragging steps together, like in the Arbor lesson. The starter tree already drives the first path.

You will add the rest, in order: wait a moment (a stand-in for picking up the game piece), drive the second path, ask the robot to aim at the goal and wait until it is aimed (with a time limit), shoot for a while, then stop.

You are done when Verify says **Paths named ToPickup and ToScore** and **Autonomous tree built**. They read the tree Arbor saves, and a failing check says which step it wanted.
say.bit: Build PickupAndScore in Arbor: path, wait, path, ask for AIM, wait for AIM (inside a Timeout), shoot, wait, back to AUTO.

say.never:
Every step answers RUNNING, SUCCESS or FAILURE each tick, and a **Sequence** moves on only when a step succeeds.

`FollowPath` stays RUNNING until the robot has arrived at the end of the path. `Sleep` stays RUNNING for the time you give it, in milliseconds (1000 = one second). `SetWantedState` asks the robot for a state, the same states the buttons ask for. Asking is instant, like pressing a button: it succeeds **at once**, before the robot has done anything.

`IsSystemState` is a question, not an action: it succeeds if the robot is in a state right now and fails if not. To **wait** for a state, put it inside a `RetryUntilSuccessful` with `num_attempts` `-1`: that asks again every tick until the answer is yes.
say.bit: FollowPath runs until the robot arrives, Sleep for its msec. SetWantedState succeeds at once; RetryUntilSuccessful around IsSystemState waits for a state.

say.never:
Asking for `SHOOT` succeeds at once: the robot is in SHOOT the moment it is asked. If the next step asked for `AUTO` straight away, the shooter would stop before it shot anything.

So after `SHOOT` comes a `Sleep` (2000 milliseconds is plenty), and only then `SetWantedState AUTO`, which stops the shooter and ends the routine.
say.bit: SHOOT succeeds at once, so Sleep about 2000 ms before asking for AUTO.

steps.title: Why the wait goes in a Timeout

say.never:
Aiming can take a while, and if something is wrong the robot might never get there, so a wait that retries forever would hang the routine. A **Timeout** wraps one step and gives it a time limit: when the time is up it stops the step and answers FAILURE. 3000 milliseconds is generous for this robot.

Right now the robot is in AIM the moment it is asked, so the wait ends at once too. Making the robot reach AIM only once it is really aimed is the next guide's job, in Java.
say.bit: Wrap the wait for AIM in a Timeout of about 3000 ms so it can't hang.

say.never: This is **Arbor**. In the **Trees** list on the left, click **PickupAndScore** to open the tree. You'll see a Sequence with one step under it: `FollowPath`, whose `trajectory` setting is `ToPickup`.

waitFor.hint: click PickupAndScore in the Trees list.

say.never: Right-click the **Sequence** box, choose **Add child…**, type `Sleep` and press **Enter**. The Sleep lands after the first `FollowPath`. Select it and type `500` in its **msec** setting on the right: half a second, a stand-in for picking up the game piece.

waitFor.hint: add a Sleep under the Sequence and set msec to 500.

say.never: Do the same with a **FollowPath**: right-click the Sequence, **Add child…**, `FollowPath`. Select it and type `ToScore` in its **trajectory** setting, spelled exactly like the path in Choreo.

waitFor.hint: add a FollowPath with trajectory ToScore.

steps.title: Ask for AIM, then wait for it

say.never:
Add a `SetWantedState` to the Sequence after the second path (right-click the Sequence, **Add child…**) and type `AIM` in its **state** setting.

After it, add a `Timeout` and set its **msec** to `3000`. Right-click the top of the Timeout's frame, choose **Add child…** and add a `RetryUntilSuccessful`; set its **num_attempts** to `-1` (keep trying). Then right-click the RetryUntilSuccessful, **Add child…**, `IsSystemState`, and set its **state** to `AIM`. Click **I did it** when the Timeout holds the wait for AIM.
say.bit: Add SetWantedState AIM, then Timeout (msec 3000) > RetryUntilSuccessful (num_attempts -1) > IsSystemState AIM.

waitFor.hint: add SetWantedState AIM and the Timeout holding the wait, then click I did it.

say.never: Last three steps, in the Sequence after the Timeout: a `SetWantedState` with `state` `SHOOT`, a `Sleep` with `msec` `2000`, and a `SetWantedState` with `state` `AUTO`. Click **I did it** when the tree ends with them.
say.bit: Add SetWantedState SHOOT, Sleep 2000, SetWantedState AUTO at the end.

waitFor.hint: add SHOOT, the Sleep and AUTO, then click I did it.

say.never: Press **Save** (or Ctrl+S). The dot next to the file name goes away. Arbor writes the tree to `deploy/autos/trees/PickupAndScore.xml`, and that file is what the robot runs. The robot reads it when it starts, so changing a tree needs **no Java and no rebuild**: save, press Start, run it.
say.bit: Save (Ctrl+S). Saved trees need no rebuild.

say.never: Open the lesson chip and press **Verify**. **Paths named ToPickup and ToScore** and **Autonomous tree built** read the tree you saved. If one fails, its message names the step it wanted.
say.bit: Press Verify. A failing check names the step it wanted.
